summary: "The Fantasy Fan, Volume 1, Number 10, June 1934" by Various is a fan magazine published in 1934. This issue belongs to the first fan magazine in weird fiction, edited by seventeen-year-old Charles Hornig. Despite its amateur status and tiny circulation of around 300 copies, it featured prestigious authors like H.P. Lovecraft, Robert E. Howard, and Clark Ashton Smith. This particular June issue notably contains Lovecraft's story "From Beyond" and continued serializing his influential essay "Supernatural Horror in Literature," cementing the magazine's importance in fantasy and horror fiction history.
